blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism
s: A pulmonary embolism happens when a blood vessel in your lungs becomes blocked.
The blockage is usually caused by a blood clot.
It can be life-threatening if not treated quickly.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism
s: Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism include:

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism
s: difficulty breathing that comes on suddenly

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism
s: chest pain that's worse when you breathe in

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism
s: coughing up blood

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Symptoms of a pulmonary embolism
s: You may also have pain and swelling in your leg (usually the calf) or arm.
The skin may become red, blue, or darker than usual – if you have black or brown skin this may be harder to see.
These are symptoms of a blood clot, also called DVT (deep vein thrombosis).

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help
s: If you have symptoms of a pulmonary embolism, you will need urgent medical help.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you have difficulty breathing which comes on suddenly

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: you feel pain in your chest or upper back

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: your heart is beating very fast

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: someone has passed out

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: These could be signs of a pulmonary embolism or another serious condition.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 and ask for an ambulance.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Immediate action required: Call 999 or go to A&E if:
s: Bring any medicines you take with you.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you're coughing up blood

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have any other symptoms you're worried about

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: If a GP thinks you've got a pulmonary embolism, you'll be sent to hospital for further tests and treatment.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: At hospital, you may be given an injection of anticoagulant medicine before you get any test results.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: Anticoagulants stop blood clots getting bigger and prevent new clots forming.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: If tests confirm you have a pulmonary embolism, you'll start anticoagulant treatment.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: This may involve anticoagulant tablets or injections, depending on the treatment that's most suitable for you.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: You'll need to have anticoagulant treatment for at least 3 months.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > Treatment for a pulmonary embolism
s: You should make a full recovery from a pulmonary embolism if it's spotted and treated early.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism
s: A pulmonary embolism usually happens when a blood clot travels up to your lungs, causing a blockage.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism
s: There are things you can do to lower your risk of getting a pulmonary embolism.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism
s: If you're staying in hospital being treated for another condition, your medical team should help reduce the risk of you getting DVT (deep vein thrombosis).

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism
s: DVT can sometimes happen on long journeys when you are sitting in the same position for a long time.
The risk of developing DVT is higher if you are travelling for 4 hours or more by plane, train or car.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism
s: There are things you can do to reduce your risk of getting DVT when travelling.

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism > Do wear loose, comfortable clothing drink water regularly walk around whenever you can bend and straighten your legs, feet and toes every 30 minutes while seated wear flight socks Don’t
s: do not sit for long periods without moving

blocks.path: Pulmonary embolism > How to reduce your risk of pulmonary embolism > Do wear loose, comfortable clothing drink water regularly walk around whenever you can bend and straighten your legs, feet and toes every 30 minutes while seated wear flight socks Don’t
s: do not drink lots of alcohol
